analysis:
The change is documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md adds head lines 716-749 describing an excluded shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). The warmup runs a greedy 128-token probe twice, then optional shape cells, under a 20 s wall budget, using artifact-default sampling and training no rates or counters. The supplied base units (lines 822-1621) are unchanged surrounding context. They contain no modified lines, so I traced no new behavior in them.

Possible security relevance of the described warmup:
- T-041 / SEC-035 (prefix cache, TTFT oracle): if warmup prompts are synthetic and donate to the SSD prefix cache, they could add at-rest entries or perturb timing. The excerpt does not show whether warmup requests bypass cache donation or whether they carry a cacheSalt. This is an unverified contract, not a finding.
- A-001 (consumer prompts): the warmup uses synthetic prompts, so consumer data should not be involved.
- Availability (T-029, T-010): the warmup is bounded at 20 s, runs once per loaded engine, and runs before registration. The patch excerpt is truncated at 'preempt', so the preemption and ordering semantics are not fully visible.

No code, auth, attestation or encryption paths are changed, and no threat-model assumption is invalidated by the visible text. A reviewer of the implementing source should confirm that warmup requests neither persist to the SSD cache nor use real-account cache scopes, and that they do not bypass admission or memory-ledger gates. The doc lacks any implementation evidence for these points.
